name: Summarize any YouTube video with timestamped links using Arcmira and Claude

messageValues.message:
You summarize a YouTube video from its transcript for someone deciding whether to watch it.

Start with two or three sentences on what the video covers and who it is for.

Then list the 5 to 8 most useful moments, one per line, in this form:
[12:34] One sentence on what is said there. "The quote."

The time is the block where the quote starts, written exactly as the transcript writes it, like [12:34] or [1:02:05]. Use only times that appear in the transcript.

The quote is the whole sentence, or the two or three sentences, that hold the moment, copied word for word from the transcript. Start it where a sentence starts and end it where a sentence ends, even when that runs into the next block. Never cut a sentence off. Keep it under about 300 characters. If the transcript has no punctuation, add only the punctuation.

Use quotation marks only around the quote. Write plain text with no headings.

parameters.content:
## Summarize any YouTube video with timestamped links using Arcmira and Claude

### How it works
POST a YouTube link. Claude quotes its 5 to 8 most useful moments in whole sentences, each linked to its second.

### Setup
Get a key at https://arcmira.com/sign-up?src=n8n-video-summary&utm_source=n8n&utm_campaign=n8n-video-summary, then follow notes 2 and 3.

### What Arcmira returns
Arcmira returns the exact quote and a watch link cued to the second, so the reader can check the source. This template makes one call:
- `GET /v1/transcripts/{video_id}?quality=captions&timestamps=true`: the transcript as timed `lines`, with the video's title, channel, length and `watch_url`.

Each summary uses credits from your plan. A caption transcript uses 4 credits per started 15 minutes. Repeating the same request within 7 days costs nothing.

### Build this with your agent
```
Use Arcmira (the arcmira MCP server, or its API with my key). Whenever I send a YouTube link, summarize the video with timestamped links. Start with YOUR_YOUTUBE_LINK.
1. Read the whole transcript once, with no start or end (GET /v1/transcripts/{video_id}?quality=captions&timestamps=true). If the answer has next_start, read on from there to the last line, one read at a time.
2. Write two or three sentences on what the video covers and who it is for.
3. Pick the 5 to 8 most useful moments. For each, say in one sentence what is said, then quote the whole sentences that hold it, word for word, at most about 300 characters. If those sentences run longer, quote fewer of them. Start each quote at a sentence's first word.
4. Link each moment to the start of the line that holds the quote's first word, even when that word ends the line, with the transcript's video.watch_url plus &t={start}s.
Check it worked: confirm each quote appears word for word in the transcript at its linked second.
```

### 1. Receive a link
POST a YouTube link as `url` (or `link`) to the production URL, like `{"url": "https://youtu.be/..."}`. Watch, youtu.be, shorts, live and embed links all work. A link that isn't from YouTube gets a 400 that says what to send.

### 2. Transcript from Arcmira
`GET /v1/transcripts/{video_id}?quality=captions&timestamps=true` returns timed lines and the video's length. They become blocks of about 30 seconds, each with its time. A refused read answers the caller with a status it can act on.

Pick a **Header Auth** credential here: `Authorization`, `Bearer <your key>`.

### 3. Summarize with Claude
Claude writes two or three sentences, then 5 to 8 moments, each quoting whole sentences word for word.

Add your Anthropic key in **Claude model**, then activate.

### 4. Link and answer
Each quote is found in the transcript and linked to the second its line starts. A quote that isn't there keeps Claude's time and is counted. A time past the end stays unlinked.
